title: Review of c07's ringswim c2 (SIBM): crescents swim on fresh seeds 25-26, but the link ring fails the 1.5 test (1.31, 1.37; moving cells median 1.04) and both seeds fuse into one band
summary: Fresh labkit runs of world_claim.py on seeds 25 and 26 (T=20000) and of the chi=0 twin on seed 25. From noise, walled cells form and swim as crescents (labkit max 6.4 and 16.2 BL; 307 and 292 cell-intervals moving >= 0.5 BL per 500 t). The link ring is weaker than claimed: aggregate L rim/core 1.31 and 1.37 (chi=0: 1.12), 15/27 and 16/28 individuals membrane-like. Per cell (ringspeed.py, labkit's radial test applied to each matched cell), moving cells have median L rim/core 1.03-1.05 against 0.59 for chi=0 cells, and only 12-15% reach 1.5; ring strength and speed are uncorrelated (Spearman 0.03, -0.02). Both seeds then fuse into a single domain-wrapping swimming band (seed 26 by t~13900, seed 25 by t~18300), so the population of individuals is not bounded on these seeds.

verdicts.limitation: B fails the rung's 1.5 rim/core test on both fresh seeds (and on 2 of the claim's 3), and the moving cells are mostly the ones without a clear ring (85-88% below 1.5 per cell), so the claim's core statement, that the moving cells carry a material ring, is not shown; the ring is present relative to chi=0 (1.04 vs 0.59 per cell) but weak. Both fresh seeds coarsen into one domain-wrapping band before t=20000 despite the waste term. Drive is a nonlocal per-body label average.
